answer: We formulate a mechanism combining dynamic opportunity-cost bonds and subgame-perfect slashing matrices to guarantee Sybil resistance. Agents face a mesa of increasing marginal costs for identity multiplication, bridged by a capital barrier that renders Sybil attacks unprofitable. In the ocean of possible strategy profiles, expected payoffs for honest participation strictly dominate those of Sybilized identities, driving Nash equilibrium convergence under adversarial multi-agent environments, thereby precluding profitable deviations via Sybilization.
